source_ref: Vo Tan Liem, Nguyen Ngoc Hien (2024) 'Customer pressure and environmental stewardship: The moderator role of perceived benefit by managers', PLOS ONE 19(7):e0306616, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0306616 (CC BY 4.0). TEXT: Table 2 'Construct reliability and validity', block 'Attitude toward the environmental [28]', rows ATE1-ATE15, read as an IMAGE via https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article/figure/image?size=large&id=10.1371/journal.pone.0306616.t002 (the wording is not in the article text; grep over the scraped HTML returns zero hits for it). OPTIONS: section 3.2 'Variables measurement' -- 'All items used a 5-point Likert scale, of which 1 = strongly disagree and 5 = strongly agree.' DATA: S1 Data (.s001, CSV), header columns ATE1..ATE15. Instrument: revised New Ecological Paradigm scale, Dunlap, Van Liere, Mertig & Jones (2000), J Soc Issues 56(3):425-442, cited as [28]. Processing script data/liem_2024_env_stewardship.py. Cached under itemtext/.cache/liem_2024_attitude_env/.
note: Clean pass with caveats. MAPPING paper_explicit, and it is a label match at both ends. Paper Table 2 prints each item prefixed with the very code the data uses ('ATE1: The Earth's carrying capacity is nearing its maximum.'), and those codes are literally the S1 Data header columns ATE1..ATE15. CODE DERIVATION is core-model pattern 1, nothing to get wrong: data/liem_2024_env_stewardship.py melts the named list [f'ATE{i}' for i in range(1,16)] with var_name='item', so the IRW item code IS the source column name -- no rename, no positional step. LEVEL 1 CHECKED AND ABSENT: the only deposit file is a bare CSV (S1 Data) whose header carries codes and no wording; there is no .sav/.xlsx and therefore no variable or value labels anywhere, so the paper's Table 2 is the highest available source. VERIFICATION (verify_liem_2024_attitude_env.R, VERIFIED): route 9 style count matching between the S1 CSV columns and the live table -- per-item response-level count vectors match cell for cell for all 15 items (e.g. ATE1 5/20/90/91/28, ATE11 4/16/64/110/40, ATE12 8/9/62/122/33), all 15 S1 vectors are mutually distinct, the 15x15 exact-match matrix has 15 hits on the diagonal and 0 off it, and the smallest off-diagonal L1 distance is 6, so the route distinguishes every item from every other item. Independent corroboration: read in code order, Table 2's wording reproduces the revised NEP's canonical alternation (odd items pro-ecological -- limits to growth, human interference, fragile balance; even items anti-ecological -- human right to modify, human ingenuity, exemptionalism), so the paper's numbering is the instrument's own. STEP 3b, clean: 15 items on 1-5 matches the paper's '15 items, based on research by Dunlap et al. (2000)' and matches no other construct in the battery (CuP 4, EMA 6, GCA 4, PB_EMA 4, CP 5, PB_CP 9), and the shipped content is general environmental attitude, not the siblings' customer pressure or accounting items. TEXT: transcribed verbatim from the Table 2 image, including its own punctuation and the missing terminal period on ATE12 ('Humans were designed to dominate the remainder of nature'); the leading 'ATEn: ' code prefix was stripped. This is an OCR-free read of an image table by eye, so it is a fallible transcription and worth a human spot-check. The wording is the authors' own rephrasing of Dunlap's NEP items rather than Dunlap's verbatim sentences, and it was shipped as-is rather than normalised to the canonical NEP wording. OPTIONS: only the two extreme anchors are published (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree); points 2-4 are unlabelled in every source and ship blank rather than padded with their own numbers. instructions blank -- the study publishes no questionnaire and no instruction text; section_prompt blank with a single trivial section_id; correct_response empty (attitude scale, no key). LANGUAGE: Vietnamese -- INFERRED, not stated. The paper never names an administration language; the respondents are 234 CEOs of Vietnamese manufacturing firms, contacted directly and by Google Form, and the authors are at Vietnamese universities. No Vietnamese wording exists in the article or its single supplement (S1 Data is integers plus ASCII codes; there is no other supporting-information file), so the 2026-09-01 fallback applies: the authors' English ships in the base fields, the four _translated columns are emitted empty, language=Vietnamese is kept as the backfill signal, and translation_source=study_supplied because nothing was translated by this project. RIGHTS: no restriction to quote. The article and S1 Data are CC BY 4.0 and the wording was copied from the article's own table; the NEP is not fee-licensed and no redistribution or non-commercial clause from Dunlap et al. could be found or quoted, so under the 2026-09-04 quote test silence is permission. DATA OBSERVATION, not a defect claim: the S1 responses are unusually regular -- 25 of 234 respondents give a strictly 4-periodic pattern across ATE1..ATE15 (r[i] == r[i mod 4]), and the same 4-cycle is visible across the other six scales in the same rows. Every ATE inter-item correlation is positive (0.35-0.86) and alpha is 0.949 despite the canonical pro/anti-NEP alternation, so either the anti-NEP items were reverse-scored before deposit or respondents did not differentiate them; the IRW table stores the S1 values unchanged either way. RETRY TEST: NO -- determinate verdict, table shipped.
public_note: The survey was fielded to CEOs of Vietnamese manufacturing firms and was in all likelihood administered in Vietnamese -- the paper does not state the language -- but the only wording published anywhere in the article or its supplement is English, so the item text shown here is the authors' own English rendering of the revised New Ecological Paradigm items rather than what respondents read; it was transcribed from Table 2, which PLOS serves only as an image. Response options carry text at the two extremes only (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree), because the paper labels no intermediate point IMPORTANT ON RESPONSE DIRECTION: the seven even-numbered items (ATE2, ATE4, ATE6, ATE8, ATE10, ATE12, ATE14) are the NEP's anti-ecological statements, but the deposit stores them ALREADY REVERSE-SCORED, so resp runs opposite to the wording printed here -- resp=5 on ATE12 ('Humans were designed to dominate the remainder of nature') encodes strong DISagreement with that statement, not agreement. The values are left as the deposit has them, per IRW's rule that response direction is not harmonised and reverse-scored items are not recoded. The source paper never states the reversal: its Table 2 reports alpha 0.949 with positive loadings on all fifteen items, which is only obtainable from reverse-scored data, and all 105 inter-item correlations in the shipped table are positive (+0.348 to +0.863) with no item-total correlation below +0.67. Careless responding was tested and does not explain it -- among the 157 respondents showing no straightlining or periodic pattern, the anti-ecological items still correlate +0.648 with the total. See irw#2118.

note: Item text = the Swedish variable labels in Soccer_supporters_raw.sav (figshare 10.17045/sthlmuni.14980251, CC BY 4.0), which label all 7 CN columns; option text = the same file's value labels (1 'Instammer verkligen inte' .. 7 'Instammer verkligen'), present for all 7 items including CN9. English in the _translated columns is the deposit codebook's own 'Text (translated to English)' / 'Answers (translated to english)' columns, verbatim (the codebook's stray unbalanced quote in the 4 = Neutral (neither agree nor disagree) anchor was closed). mapping_basis=data_labels and the code derivation is pattern 1 (core model 3): data/lindstrom2021_soccer.py melts the raw columns by name (SCALES['collective_narcissism'] = CN3..CN9) so the IRW item code IS the .sav column name -- no positional step, nothing to infer. Deviations disclosed: .sav variable labels preferred over the codebook Text column where the two differ by typo/punctuation. RENAMED 2026-09-08 (irw#2107): this table shipped as lindstrom2021_conscientiousness, a name this project invented by reading the CN prefix as Conscientiousness. The deposit's own codebook heads the block 'Collective narcissism;Scale (7 items);CN3' and lists no conscientiousness scale at all. Renamed to lindstrom2021_collective_narcissism; the item text was never published, so it was replaced in the irw_text_2 draft rather than withdrawn. RIGHTS CHECKED 2026-09-08 (irw#2107 follow-up), replacing the availability_audit row, which cleared this table on the reasoning that 'Conscientiousness is a standard HEXACO-PI-R subscale and the full HEXACO item pool is freely published' -- a ruling about an instrument this table does not contain. The real instrument is the Collective Narcissism Scale (Golec de Zavala, Cichocka, Eidelson & Jayawickreme, 2009, JPSP 97(6):1074-1096); CN3..CN9 are its items 3-9, confirmed item by item against the published wording (CN4 'Hammarby maste fa den respekt vi fortjanar' = 'I insist upon my group getting the respect that is due to it'; CN7R = the scale's reverse-scored item 7). NO STATED RESTRICTION IS QUOTABLE from the originator: the 2009 article carries only an APA article notice, which governs the article and not the instrument (the same distinction already applied to pezzuti_2025_coolpeople_main_nfc); there is no licence page, permission-required statement, distribution notice or watermark; and third-party measure repositories reproduce the items with no terms attached. Under the 2026-09-04 rule the block fires on a quotable restriction and not on an inference, and explicitly does not fire because a scale is copyrighted or is reproduced without an explicit grant. WEIGHED AND REJECTED as a restriction: Golec de Zavala's own 2023 book (Goldsmiths OA, 9781003296577) is CC-BY-NC-ND 4.0, but that is Taylor & Francis's licence on the book, not an instrument-distribution notice, and it postdates the scale by 13 years -- the same reasoning by which an APA article notice does not restrict the instrument it prints. Separately, what IRW ships here is not the English original at all: it is Lindstrom's Swedish Hammarby-referent adaptation, taken from her own CC BY 4.0 figshare deposit's .sav variable labels.
